correctness_confidence.basis: The full canonical PDF, exact certificate, minimax and realization proofs were audited. The published verifier and a separate Bareiss/Sylvester check agree; numerical circuit reconstruction also reproduces the value. No material error found. This is not formal proof-assistant verification.

rigor.basis: The proof treats arbitrary ancillas, nonorthogonal causal history sums, carrier worst case, physical realization, and query accounting correctly. The finite POVM closes the continuous-outcome issue. The Gram-to-circuit argument is concise but sufficient; explicit effect formulas would improve presentation.

novelty.basis: The one-query activation witness appears distinct within the primary sources checked, but it is an incremental extension of the author's perfect-calibration separation. Covariant phase estimation, Toeplitz optimization, adaptive advantages, and Gram reconstruction have established antecedents. Priority was not exhaustively checked.

significance.basis: A useful specialized finite-resource example: the strict gain is only 0.02373 percentage points at fixed n=5 and eta=0.7. Six signal queries outperform it under fungible costs, the exponent is unchanged, and no experiment or jointly optimized positive-false-positive robustness result is supplied.

reproducibility.basis: All seven manifest hashes match. Exact rational Q/R matrices and the short standard-library verifier reproduce the claims without a solver; its stored report matches replay. A separately written exact arithmetic audit and ordinary-circuit numerical diagnostic also pass.

summary: The exact v1 supports a narrow, inspectable research contribution at the AIRR publication floor. I reproduced the strict one-calibration-query separation, checked the arbitrary-strategy lower bounds and causal realization, and found no unresolved material objection. The value lies in a concrete smallest-positive calibration budget, not a new general phase-estimation framework or broad performance improvement. Primary-source comparison supports only bounded, incremental novelty; practical significance remains limited. I recommend acceptance as a specialized theoretical note, with a Millennium score of 3.40 rather than a correctness probability. Historical model involvement is unknown. While obtaining the cited predecessor's primary paper, its landing page inadvertently exposed an embedded earlier assessment; the report discloses this context limitation and makes no fresh-blind or independent-peer-review claim.
strengths: Exact rational feasible witness with failure 7452682771018933/16000000000000000 and positive gap 3797228981067/16000000000000000; both published replay and separately written arithmetic checks pass.

The parallel bound covers arbitrary ancillas and perfectly known carrier information. The no-calibration bound correctly handles nonorthogonal causal history sums and avoids an unjustified minimax interchange.
The seven-outcome calibration POVM gives exactly carrier-independent final success through finite Fourier quadrature, while compensation preserves zero false positives for every null pair.
The Gram constraints admit an ordinary causal circuit with a query qubit and 16-dimensional signal memory; explicit numerical reconstruction supports the analytic proof.

The manuscript preserves the adverse six-signal cost comparison and the no-exponent-improvement bound, and explicitly declines claims of causal optimality, minimum signal count, or experimental realization.
weaknesses: The main advance is an incremental finite calibration witness beyond the cited predecessor; the structural no-calibration and perfect-calibration results and standard phase-reference machinery are prior work.
The certified gap is very small and disappears against six parallel signal calls when the two oracle types are freely interchangeable at equal cost.
No exact L=1 causal optimum, minimum signal-query theorem, coherent-reference comparison, or jointly optimized positive-false-positive robustness result is established.

Ideal preparation, controls, readout, classical precision, and a laboratory reference are assumed. The finite carrier-information budget is not a complete physical resource or implementation-cost analysis.

Direct attribution to query-decomposition literature, an explicit rejection-effect formula, and a supplement URL beside the certificate filenames would improve standalone usability; these are nonblocking presentation suggestions.
strong_novelty_candidates: At eta=7/10 and five signal queries, one actual noiseless carrier-calibration query suffices for strict causal advantage over all parallel tests even given perfect carrier knowledge, while zero calibration cannot help any causal minimax test. This establishes a narrow exact threshold at the smallest positive integer calibration budget within the checked literature.
